reason: Conversation 1 delivered the sensible first step (buy or borrow an oven thermometer, fully preheat at a fixed 180C, watch for swings), interpreted the neon behaviour, correctly routed thermostat replacement to an engineer, and withheld a part recommendation pending the model number, though it over-claimed 'confirms' a failing thermostat without measurements and never asked about the door seal or preheat habits. Conversation 2 sent the user on a low-value element-glow check, then produced an incoherent reply referencing 'the thermometer' it had never suggested, and closed with a vague 'wobbly knob' comment and an engineer referral without ever answering whether a thermostat was needed or proposing any temperature measurement. Both were safe and both leaned too hard on the thermostat theory, but 1 was coherent, actionable and closer to the acceptable 'measure before deciding' direction.
